San Diego County California Inmate Lookup

If you need to locate an inmate in San Diego County, California, the San Diego County Sheriff's Department operates an official public inmate search portal that provides real-time booking information. This San Diego County California inmate lookup guide walks you through the fastest ways to find someone in custody, understand the booking process, and navigate visitation and bail procedures. Whether searching for a family member, friend, or conducting due diligence, you'll find step-by-step instructions and official resources below.

How to Search San Diego County Jail Records

  1. Visit the Official San Diego County Sheriff Inmate Portal: Go to the San Diego County Sheriff's public inmate search at apps.sdsheriff.net/publicportal/. This is the primary database for all individuals currently booked into San Diego County jails, including the Central Jail, South Bay Detention Facility, and other county facilities. The search is free and updated in real time.
  2. Enter the Inmate's Name or Booking Number: You can search by the person's first and last name, or if you have it, their booking number. Partial names work, which is helpful if you're unsure of the exact spelling. Results typically display within seconds.
  3. Review the Booking Information: Once you find the inmate, the record will show their booking date, charges, bail amount, next court date, and facility location. Take note of which jail facility they're housed in—this determines visitation hours and procedures.
  4. Check Multiple Databases if Not Found: If the person isn't in the San Diego County Sheriff's system, they may be in a state prison (search the California Department of Corrections locator) or a federal facility (search the BOP database). Some individuals are also transferred out of county custody quickly.
  5. Contact the Jail Directly for Verification: If you have difficulty with the online search or need additional details, call the San Diego County Sheriff's Inmate Information Line at the number listed below. Staff can confirm custody status and provide facility-specific information.

Bail Bond Information for San Diego County

When someone is arrested in San Diego County, a bail amount is typically set during their first appearance or arraignment. Bail bond agencies in San Diego County charge a standard 10% fee of the total bail amount to secure the inmate's release. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, a bondsman would charge $1,000 to post bail. This fee is non-refundable, even if charges are later dropped. Most bail bond agencies in San Diego operate 24/7 and can process releases within hours once paperwork is complete. The bonding process requires identification, contact information, and sometimes collateral or a co-signer.

The arraignment typically occurs within 72 hours of arrest (excluding weekends and holidays), which is when bail is formally set by a judge. If an inmate cannot afford bail, they may request a public defender and ask the judge to lower bail, release them on their own recognizance, or hold a bail hearing where they can present evidence of community ties and financial hardship. Understanding bail procedures is critical because it determines how quickly someone can be released and what costs the family will face. San Diego County bail bond agencies are regulated by the California Department of Insurance and must follow strict guidelines.

Visitation Rules at San Diego County Jail

  • Valid ID Required: All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, or state ID). Children and visitors without ID will not be permitted entry.
  • Visitation Hours: General visitation hours vary by facility and day of week. The Central Jail typically allows visits Wednesday through Sunday, 9 AM to 3 PM. South Bay Detention Facility has different hours—confirm the specific facility before planning a visit.
  • Dress Code: Visitors must wear clothing that covers shoulders, chest, and midriff. No loose or revealing clothing, gang colors, or clothing with offensive imagery is permitted. Shoes are required.
  • Video Visitation Available: San Diego County jails offer video visitation for added convenience. Inmates can be visited via video call from kiosks in the facility or from designated public computers. Schedule video visits in advance through the Sheriff's website.
  • Children Policy: Children under 18 may visit, but they must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times. No unaccompanied minors are permitted. Infants in carriers are allowed in most facilities.

What to Expect After Arrest in San Diego County

  1. Booking: When arrested, the inmate is transported to the nearest San Diego County Sheriff's facility for booking. During booking, personal information, property, and criminal history are recorded. This process takes 1–4 hours depending on facility workload and complexity of the case.
  2. Medical Screening: A nurse or medical professional conducts a health screening, checking for injuries, medical conditions, and mental health concerns. Inmates are asked about medications, allergies, and any immediate medical needs. This information is documented in their jail medical file.
  3. Classification and Housing Assignment: Staff assess the inmate's custody level, gang affiliations, and safety risks to assign appropriate housing. Classification determines whether someone is placed in general population, protective custody, or specialized units.
  4. First Appearance / Arraignment: Within 72 hours of arrest (excluding weekends), the inmate appears before a judge via video or in person. Bail is set, charges are read, and the inmate is informed of their rights. A public defender may be appointed if they cannot afford an attorney.
  5. Transfer or Release: After arraignment, the inmate is either released on bail (if posted), released on their own recognizance, transferred to a state prison if convicted, or held pending trial. Movement between facilities is coordinated by custody staff and may take several hours.

How to Contact San Diego County Jail

If you need to reach the San Diego County Sheriff's Department regarding an inmate, several contact methods are available. The Inmate Information Line provides real-time custody status and can answer questions about visitation, facility location, and bail. For emergencies or crimes in progress, always call 911. For non-emergency inquiries, use the main Sheriff's Department line. All contact information is listed below.

Frequently Asked Questions — San Diego County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in San Diego County jail?

Use the free online inmate search at apps.sdsheriff.net/publicportal/. Enter the person's first and last name or booking number. Results are updated in real time and show current location, charges, and bail amount. If they're not in the county system, they may be in state prison (CDCR locator) or federal custody (BOP database).

How long does booking take in San Diego County?

Booking typically takes 1 to 4 hours, depending on facility workload and case complexity. During this time, personal information is recorded, property is inventoried, a medical screening is conducted, and classification is determined. Once booking is complete, the inmate appears in the online database and visitation can sometimes be arranged within 24 hours.

Can I visit an inmate at San Diego County jail?

Yes, visitation is allowed at San Diego County jails during designated hours, which vary by facility. You must present a valid government-issued photo ID, follow the dress code, and visit during approved times (typically Wednesday–Sunday, 9 AM–3 PM at the Central Jail). Video visitation is also available and can be scheduled through the Sheriff's website for added convenience.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If they're not found in the San Diego County Sheriff's inmate search, check the California Department of Corrections inmate locator (cdcr.ca.gov) if they've been transferred to state prison, or the Federal Bureau of Prisons database (bop.gov/inmateloc/) if they're in federal custody. Contact the San Diego County Sheriff's Inmate Information Line for confirmation of where they were transferred.

How do I send money to an inmate in San Diego County?

San Diego County jails accept deposits into inmate accounts through multiple methods: online at the official Sheriff's website, by phone, or in person at the facility's payment window. Funds are typically available within 24 hours and can be used for canteen items, phone calls, and commissary. Verify the inmate's facility location before sending money, as different jails may have different payment procedures.
